variants.headline: A friend in the {{era}}: {{civilization}}
body: The crossing from the {{former}} into the {{era}} is complete in {{civilization}}, a friend of our nation. In their towns, the schoolteachers have hung new charts beside the old ones, and the youngest pupils are learning them by heart. Their parents are hearing the new words at supper.

variants.headline: A friendly power enters the {{era}}
body: A friend of our nation has crossed from the {{former}} into the {{era}}, and the name has not reached us. The couriers brought the age before they brought the name.

variants.headline: A friend crosses into the {{era}}
body: Letters from the friendly courts bring word that {{civilization}} has lately passed from the {{former}} into the {{era}}. We offer congratulations without hesitation: a friend grown stronger in the learning of the age makes a better customer, a better teacher and a steadier neighbor, and we welcome all three.

variants.headline: A new age in {{civilization}}, they say
body: The drovers brought it over the pass before any letter could: {{civilization}} has crossed into the {{era}}. They say the bells in their towns rang all evening.

variants.headline: Of {{civilization}}'s entry into the {{era}}
body: It is recorded that {{civilization}}, whose nearest city stands {{distance}} tiles from our own, left the {{former}} in this season and entered the {{era}}. At the school there, the keeper of the books set a fresh sheet at the head of the year's accounts.

variants.headline: What a friend's new era means
body: Our friend has crossed from the {{former}} into the {{era}}. A professor here has asked an old colleague there for permission to bring students to his lectures. A visit like that can bring home lessons our scholars would otherwise have to wait to read.

variants.headline: New learning on the frontier: {{tech}}
body: Word from the frontier: {{tech}} is now known in {{team}}, whose cities stand close to ours. The border clerks have begun asking travelers what they have heard of it, and paying for the answers.

variants.headline: New knowledge in {{team}}: {{tech}}
body: Word from abroad: {{tech}} now appears on the learned rolls of {{team}}. Their bookbinders have been asked for another copy before the first is dry.

variants.headline: A neighbor's new learning
body: What a neighbor knows changes what a neighbor can do. {{team}}, whose lands run along ours, now knows {{tech}}. Somewhere across the border a workshop is already trying it out. The ledger of the age has a new entry, not in our handwriting.

variants.headline: Notice to the learned: {{tech}} abroad
body: The printers advise the learned that the art of {{tech}} is now practiced by {{team}}, whose cities stand near ours. The fact is set down as it arrived, and correction is invited from any scholar who can show otherwise.

variants.headline: New learning across the fence
body: At the border stalls the morning's argument was {{tech}}. The knife-grinder swore it would change everything and could not say what. By noon the market agreed on one thing only: it is {{team}}'s now, and the fence has never once stopped a rumor.

variants.headline: The lamp next door
body: Next door the lamp burns bright and late. {{tech}} is the word at our gate.

variants.headline: Our nation enters the {{era}}
body: Our nation has entered the {{era}}. A joiner who began as an apprentice in the old era says she has started putting aside worn tools for pupils who want to see how their grandparents worked.

variants.headline: Hear it! The {{era}} is ours
body: Hear it, hear it, people of the {{era}}! The old age is done with us, and the new one is ours. Every town, every farm, every one of us stands in it together. Say it in the streets and say it again: the {{era}} is ours!

variants.headline: The {{era}} begins tonight
body: The nation has entered the {{era}}. We asked a schoolteacher what he would tell his pupils. "I want to know what they expect to be able to do that I can't," he said.

variants.headline: The record of our passage into the {{era}}
body: In this year it was given to the nation to pass out of the former age and into the {{era}}. The scribes set it down with thanks. In the shrines the lamps will burn late this season; heaven carried us here, and the wardens mean to say so.

variants.headline: The bells rang all morning
body: Madam Editor, the bells rang all morning for our entry into the {{era}}, and already I hear neighbors calling it the world turning. Worlds do not turn by themselves. This crossing was planned, paid for and finished by people who will never stand on a balcony about it, and the city owes them its thanks.

variants.headline: The scholars finish {{tech}}
body: Our scholars have finished {{tech}}. The first copy went to the council, the second to the printers, and the third is already missing from the shelf.

variants.headline: Who can teach {{tech}} next?
body: Our researchers have completed their work on {{tech}}. A teacher who has been following it has started copying notes for colleagues who couldn't attend the demonstrations. A finding that can be taught in another town can outlast the team that made it.

variants.headline: One more for the home team
body: Our scholars just finished {{tech}}. No parade, no speech, no day off. Just one more thing this country can do that it couldn't last week.

variants.headline: Notice: {{tech}} is finished
body: The printers are advised that our scholars have brought {{tech}} to completion. The {{era}} continues what earlier ages began; each generation takes up the work where the last one laid it down, and this piece is now whole.

variants.headline: At the market, the word is {{tech}}
body: The fish-seller at the morning market had it before the mayor's man did: our scholars have finished {{tech}}. What it does, nobody at the stalls could say. That it was ours, nobody needed telling twice.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} crosses into the {{era}}
body: The {{former}} has given way to the {{era}} in {{civilization}}. One merchant has asked her agent there to send samples before she promises customers what will be in her next shipment.

variants.headline: A rival power enters the {{era}}
body: A power that is neither our friend nor our ally has crossed from the {{former}} into the {{era}}. The dispatches that carried the news managed to lose the name on the way.

variants.headline: A rival leaves the {{former}}
body: Advices from abroad state that {{civilization}}, no particular friend of ours, has lately passed from the {{former}} into the {{era}}. We report the crossing as it reached us. Whether it deserves congratulation or watchfulness we leave to readers better acquainted with that quarter.

variants.headline: Up the road, a new era
body: The map says nothing has changed. The map is wrong: {{civilization}} has crossed into the {{era}}, and its nearest city stands {{distance}} tiles from ours. The border has not moved, but the country behind it just did.

variants.headline: It is told of {{civilization}}
body: It is told that in {{civilization}} the old calendars were not thrown away but shelved, and the new count begins with the {{era}}. What the old age cost them, the tellers do not say.

variants.headline: A rival enters the {{era}}. And us?
body: Citizens! {{civilization}} has entered the {{era}}, and somewhere their ministers are being asked what it cost them. Ask ours the same question: what are we paying, and for which age? A government that cannot say is paying more than it admits.

variants.headline: First in learning: {{civilization}}
body: First place in research now goes to {{civilization}}, with {{count}} known technologies. A bookseller says customers buying the latest journal from that country have started asking when a translation will come out.

variants.headline: A new nation stands first in learning
body: A new nation has reached first place in research, with {{count}} known technologies. The librarian at one reading room says patrons have begun asking if they can borrow the foreign journals overnight.

variants.headline: The learning count, restated
body: First in learning: {{civilization}}
Arts and sciences held: {{count}}
Nations ahead of it: none

variants.headline: First place, shared
body: The count says {{civilization}} leads the world in learning with {{count}} arts and sciences. The count also says somebody matched them. The podium was built for one.

variants.headline: Two ways to count learning
body: The nation first in the tally holds {{count}} arts and sciences. One art may have passed through several generations of masters while another has scarcely left the school, yet each adds one to the sum. A rival lower in the tally may have trained more people in the arts the two nations share.
